lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Skill model: meal and supply planning at scale

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic meal and supply planning at scale task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Using the same fictional one-person household and its invented grocery-budget slice, the learner plans seven days of meals, builds a matching shopping list sorted into staples versus perishables, and checks the list's estimated fictional cost against the budget slice.
safetyNotes: All food items, quantities, and prices in this plan are invented for practice; no real household's actual food budget or real prices are required.
materials: adult-or-local: the fictional household budget from the previous lesson
learner-local: paper or a notes/spreadsheet document

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l02-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l02-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l02-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l02-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: What was harder than expected about planning a full week of meals at once instead of day by day?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g12-u02-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Plan-to-list consistency: The shopping list is clearly derived from the seven days of planned meals. | Budget fit: The estimated cost is compared to the budget slice, and any gap is named. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner replan the week assuming their fictional grocery budget slice is cut by a third, and explain what strategy they used to still cover seven days.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic meal and supply planning at scale task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.elapsedWindow: Up to seven days; use only the check-ins explicitly named in the task
duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: the fictional household budget from the previous lesson
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

resources.title: meal and supply planning at scale worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Using the same fictional one-person household and its invented grocery-budget slice, the learner plans seven days of meals, builds a matching shopping list sorted into staples versus perishables, and checks the list's estimated fictional cost against the budget slice.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact meal and supply planning at scale decision or action.
Model move 2: Before planning, list what tends to go wrong with meal planning if you don't do it at all.
Model move 3: Plan seven days of meals for your fictional household and sort a matching shopping list into staples and perishables.

Model check: Plan-to-list consistency: The shopping list is clearly derived from the seven days of planned meals. | Budget fit: The estimated cost is compared to the budget slice, and any gap is named.

resources.title: meal and supply planning at scale action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for meal and supply planning at scale.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: meal and supply planning at scale coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Using the same fictional one-person household and its invented grocery-budget slice, the learner plans seven days of meals, builds a matching shopping list sorted into staples versus perishables, and checks the list's estimated fictional cost against the budget slice.
Coach direction: Before planning, list what tends to go wrong with meal planning if you don't do it at all.
Learner prompt: What is one problem that happens when someone buys groceries without any plan at all?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: meal and supply planning at scale complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Plan seven days of meals for your fictional household and sort a matching shopping list into staples and perishables.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I planned meals or meal types for all seven days.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I built a shopping list sorted into staples (last a while) and perishables (need to be used soon).
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: meal and supply planning at scale minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: What was harder than expected about planning a full week of meals at once instead of day by day?

Success checks: Plan-to-list consistency: The shopping list is clearly derived from the seven days of planned meals. | Budget fit: The estimated cost is compared to the budget slice, and any gap is named.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: meal and supply planning at scale supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g12-u02-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional meal and supply planning at scale condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Plan-to-list consistency: The shopping list is clearly derived from the seven days of planned meals. | Budget fit: The estimated cost is compared to the budget slice, and any gap is named..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
